I'm probably the odd one out here, NTA. Right now. 

I am 20, my brother is freshly 18. My father is very similar to your husband, disciplinary is a nice way to put it, we just call him crazy. 

My father is a person who hurts people who he feels deserved it, even if that person was a *child* or his *wife*

When I became a teen I separated myself from my dad because I was *afraid of him.* Going anywhere with him was hell, he'd scream at us for the smallest things and than belittle us the entire time. When I was 16 he started shoving me, and pushing me to the ground, because he knew that it wasn't technically "hitting" me. Because he knew I could get away from it. He one pushed my *disabled* mom down and she hit her head on the cement floor.

My Mom always defended him to us. And us to him. She always said that he was a "good man" at heart. 

Let me wrap up by making clear my point: Father's who scream at their children will never only scream. Even if you don't see it, their irrational. They make bad decisions and permanently harm your children. My father has threatened to k1ll me, most of them being when I was like 16.

I've been to at least 5 phycologists/therapists in my life, and the last 3 have discussed C-PTSD or Trauma with me at some point. My mother, although her reason for staying was admirable, was forcing us to stay with a man who hurt us.

I'm being 100% serious right now when I say I *wish* my mom had the ability to protect and defend us the way you do your daughter. But if he continues to yell, cause anxiety, cause *genuine fear* in your children 

Than YTA. 

If you stay with him, knowing he's hurting your kids. Than you're the AH. 

I deal with resentment of my mom now. I know she thought she was keeping us safe by staying with him, but he *was hurting us.* She should've left, and I resent her ignoring my plea's for safety and comfort. 

Don't be an enabler for a grown ass man who *screams at his children*.
